title: SpruceGate constraint + objection sandbox
content:
Quick context: SpruceGate is a mid-market logistics SaaS (warehouse + last-mile routing). Came up via inbound form — asked about "model hosting" and "data residency". Seemed price-sensitive but tech-forward (engineering org ~15). Primary contact: Luke Harrow (Head of Platform). Secondary: Maya Chen (Head of Ops).

Why this is interesting (quick thesis):
- Use cases fit Redwood: automated driver instructions & incident summarization, customer notifications (templated generation), and internal ops Q&A (embedding search over SOPs).
- Latency matter: they run mobile devices at edge with intermittent connectivity; occasional offline caching + short high-availability bursts.
- Security/regulatory: contracts mention customer PII (addresses, phone). They asked explicitly about encryption at rest and key control.

Key constraints / red flags to validate on discovery call:
1) Data residency — must be within US only (legal requirement for some customers).
2) Latency SLO per mobile request: target 300ms p95 for short prompts (driver instruction). If they expect sub-100ms we will need to qualify device-vs-server routing.
3) Cost sensitivity — procurement pref on price per 1M tokens; wants to know saving vs other providers.
4) Model determinism / hallucinations — Ops team cannot have hallucinated routing instructions. Need guardrails.
5) Integration effort — they use Go backend + k8s (EKS), expect minimal infra lift for pilot.

Champion & org map (rough):
- Luke Harrow (Platform) — champion, cares about infra alignment, SLOs, SDK simplicity.
- Maya Chen (Ops/Product) — cares about output accuracy, safety, evals.
- Legal (unknown) — will require DPA + possibly SOC2.
- Procurement (unknown) — will push on committed minimums.

Initial pitch hooks (short):
- "Ship reliable inference with predictable latency and costs" — lead with Dedicated + Optimize recommendations.
- Emphasize Private (VPC) option for data residency + KMS support — call out HSM/KMS integrations.
- Show measurable unit economics: batching + KV caching -> up to 3–4x token savings for templated driver prompts.

Cold / follow-up email sequence (draft snippets):
1) Short intro (50–80 words): reference inbound, call out one clear pain (driver instructions latency + hallucination risk), suggest 20-min call to show short pilot plan (no infra change).
2) Followup w/ value add: one-pager on "driver instruction pilot" (bullets: dataset, eval, p95 target, fallback policy), include quick cost estimate.
3) Technical note to Luke: SDK + EKS patterns, sample config for Dedicated pool + autoscale (attach gist link).
4) Final nudge: client story (similar logistics customer reduced token cost 3.2x and cut p95 from 1.2s -> 310ms).

Call outline (20 min):
- 0–3m: intros, confirm attendees and timeline.
- 3–7m: understand concrete flows for driver instructions (sample prompt, frequency, typical seq len).
- 7–12m: map constraints (latency target, data residency, fallback requirements).
- 12–17m: present 30-day pilot plan: hosted PoC -> Dedicated trial -> Private if needed. Show metrics: latency, cost, error handling, rollout plan.
- 17–20m: next steps, decision owner, procurement timeline.

Objection library (quick scripts):
- "We can't risk hallucinations" -> "We lock down templates + run evals against historical transcripts; fallback to rule-based when confidence low. Redwood Optimize can monitor eval drift and alert. We'll run a pre-flight eval using your sample prompts and historical outputs — showing expected FP/false halluc rate before any rollout." 
- "Your price is higher than X" -> "We can model end-to-end unit economics: after batching, caching, and routing to cheaper model variants for non-sensitive traffic, typical customers see 30–60% lower per-request costs versus naïve per-token pricing. I can run a cost compare with 1 week of sample logs." 
- "We require data never leave our VPC" -> "Private deployment is designed for that — control plane options and on-prem packages exist. We can propose an initial Dedicated-in-VPC design so logs & tokens never leave your network." 
- "We already have internal infra" -> "We integrate via standard SDKs and offer a managed Dedicated pool that reduces ops lift; many customers keep model weights in their control while Redwood manages serving and autoscaling." 

Experiment ideas to shorten procurement:
- 30-day technical spike limited to 2 endpoints: (1) templated instruction generator, (2) embedding-based SOP search. Deliverables: latency report, cost model, hallucination eval.
- Offer a 90-day trial credit on Dedicated capacity in exchange for a short case study (especially if they have measurable ops KPIs).

Notes to self / action items:
- Prep sample cost model: need 7 days of sample logs from Luke (approx 300k prompts / month). Build a quick spreadsheet (open question: tokenization assumptions for short templated prompts). Owner: Noah.
- Draft legal ask: DPA + SOC2 evidence pack. Ritu to circle back with security org.
- Create small demo app (Go example) showing SDK + fallback routing using Llama-2 family + quantization suggestions from Optimize. Link to gist in follow-up.
- Schedule discovery: aim for week of 11/17.

Open questions to confirm on call:
1) Do driver devices run inference locally sometimes? If yes, what's the mobile SDK story?
2) Which cloud region constraints (US-east only? specific states)?
3) Who signs procurement and typical PO thresholds?
4) Any existing contracts with model vendors (clauses about model weights / fine-tuning)?

Tone / positioning notes (internal):
- Avoid 'model vendor' debate at first — focus on operational risk (latency, reliability, predictability).
- Use concrete metrics (p95, cost per 10k requests) rather than high-level claims.
- Keep legal/security conversation visible early — bring Ritu once they confirm residency requirements.

Rough meeting invite text (to use after alignment):
"Luke — thanks for the inbound. I put together a 20-min plan to align on latency targets and a lightweight 30-day pilot we can run with minimal infra lift. Proposed slots: Tue/Wed 11/17–11/18. Agenda: 1) current flow + constraints, 2) quick pilot plan, 3) next steps. Can you invite Maya + one engineer?

-- Ava
